newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi stocks drop sharply at close. [CORRECTED 12:50 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Delhi stocks drop sharply at close. [CORRECTED 12:50 GMT]

text.p: Delhi share prices closed sharply lower on Tuesday on heavy selling by foreign financial institutions and speculators, brokers said.
The bourse's benchmark index closed 22.42 points, or 2.47 percent lower at 884.84 points.
Traders said they were keeping their options limited ahead of a United Front (UF) steering committee meeting to discuss an imminent petroleum products price hike.
The decision making steering-committee is scheduled to meet on Thursday (corrects from Wednesday) to thrash out the issue of fuel price hike.
At the end of March, the government owed $4.3 billion to state oil firms for selling their products below world prices.
"Players offloaded their positions ahead of the UF meeting on petroleum prices," said one broker.
ITC fell 28.15 rupees to 540.85 on heavy selling by foreign investors, brokers said.
Reliance Industries lost seven rupees to 364.25.
State Bank of India declined 4.95 rupees to 319.
Bajaj Auto dropped 35.50 rupees lower at 833.50.
Larsen and Toubro slipped 11.15 rupees to 261.25.
